reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that predictive uncertainty under dataset shift cannot be reliably assessed through i.i.d. validation alone. The paper introduces a rigorous framework where models are evaluated not only on in-distribution performance but also under increasingly severe distributional shifts. This challenges the assumption that post-hoc calibration techniques such as temperature scaling generalize. Instead, it shows that ensembles maintain superior calibration properties under shift. The mathematical formulation uses metrics like Brier Score, Expected Calibration Error (ECE), and Negative Log-Likelihood (NLL) to quantify this behavior. These metrics are defined over confidence bins and provide a structured way to assess reliability under perturbations. In GSE context, this translates into a need for dynamic recalibration protocols that account for evolving game conditions—such as QB injuries or weather changes—where static calibration fails. The shift-stress protocol becomes essential for validating models before deployment in live environments.
